subject: Genetics
title: Population Genomics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Population Genomics.

hook.text: Iceland sequenced its entire population. The UK sequenced 500,000 people. Genomics went from one genome to millions.

buildup.text: The UK Biobank links genomes to health records, diet, and lifestyle. It's a goldmine for discovering gene-disease links.

discovery.text: deCODE in Iceland found that every Icelander is related within 10 generations. Small populations reveal rare variants.

twist.text: Most genomic databases are 80% European. Discoveries may not apply to other populations. Bias persists at scale.

climax.text: The All of Us program aims to sequence 1 million diverse Americans. Inclusion is catching up—slowly.

punchline.text: Genomics works best when it includes everyone.

quiz.question: What percentage of genomic databases are of European descent?
